summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan) by itself in adults with advanced gastrointestinal cancers. Rina-S is given through an IV, and each cycle lasts 21 days. The average treatment period is expected to be about 12 months, and participants may continue while the cancer stays the same or gets better and there are no serious problems. The main outcome is not stated; this is a Phase 2 study.
summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 2 evalúa Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan) por sí solo en personas con cánceres gastrointestinales avanzados. Rina-S se administra por vía intravenosa, y cada ciclo dura 21 días. Se espera que el tratamiento dure en promedio unos 12 meses, y los participantes pueden seguir recibiéndolo mientras el cáncer se mantenga igual o mejore y no haya problemas graves. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; es un estudio de Fase 2.
who_for: Confirmed gastrointestinal cancer that has spread (metastatic) or cannot be removed by surgery with curative intent.
Measurable disease on imaging, and imaging shows the disease has grown after the most recent treatment.
ECOG performance status of 0 or 1 and life expectancy of at least 3 months.
Able to provide a newly obtained or archival tumor tissue sample.
Adequate organ and bone marrow function based on laboratory tests before Rina-S.
not_for: Non-cancer bowel conditions such as ulcerative colitis, inflammatory bowel disease, or diarrhea above grade 1.
Recent significant GI bleeding, fistula, abscess, or perforation, or current cancer-related ulcers.
Any other past or current cancer, or residual disease from a previous cancer.
Unstable or symptomatic central nervous system metastases, or a history of carcinomatous meningitis.
Prior treatment with a topoisomerase-1 inhibitor antibody-drug conjugate, or anticancer treatment within 28 days before the first dose.
